name: MA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with a +15 partisan lean
Incumbent Stephen Lynch running with a large financial advantage
Republican opponent Robert Burke has negligible fundraising and negative cash on hand
Prediction markets price Lynch at roughly 97% to win
model.rationale: Lynch holds a deep-blue Boston-area seat with a +15 Democratic lean, has raised over $900,000, and faces a Republican opponent with essentially no money and negative cash on hand. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy incumbent win, so the forecast stays at a Safe D rating with a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending against Lynch or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though it would still likely leave him favored.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' 8th District is a solidly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of about 15 points toward Democrats. Stephen Lynch, the longtime incumbent, is running for reelection and enters the general election with a commanding financial position: roughly $910,000 raised and more than $640,000 on hand, though outside groups have spent about $214,000 opposing him.

His Republican opponent, Robert Burke, has raised only about $1,500 and reports negative cash on hand, leaving him with no visible resources to contest the race. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but shows no fundraising activity. With no public polling and no expert ratings available, the picture rests on the district's fundamentals, the incumbent's advantages, and prediction markets, which price Lynch's chances at about 97 percent. Everything points to a comfortable incumbent victory.
